title: The Cold Echo
premise: Ansel Oyelaran, the fourth clone of a murdered surveyor, is sent to dying colony Meridian-9 to close a case no one wants solved, cataloguing its slow abandonment while hiding his own nature. When the long-lost ship Cassiopeia returns with its crew aged backward into children who remember their own deaths, Ansel realizes the original's murder and the colony's decay are symptoms of the same temporal weapon. Pursued by the corporation that built him, he races to the dead-space relay to broadcast proof before his own memory buffer is wiped. He reaches it, but transmitting costs him every stored memory of the original—leaving him finally, irrevocably himself.
about_author: Jonah Brightwater is the pen name of a former radio telescope technician who spent six winters at an Arctic listening station, where the silence between signals taught him more about people than the signals did. The Cold Echo is his third novel and the first written entirely by hand during station blackouts.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dying Place
chapters.summary: Ansel arrives at Meridian-9 under corporate orders to document the colony's closure and quietly shelve the original's murder file. Through his POV we see empty hydroponics bays and residents who won't meet his eyes. The emotional beat is quiet dread: everyone here seems to recognize something in his face that he doesn't yet understand himself.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept the Lights
chapters.summary: Ansel interviews Sefa Idris, the last engineer maintaining the relay uplink, who claims the original visited her the night he died. His POV reveals gaps in his inherited memories—deliberate ones. The beat is uneasy intimacy: she treats him like a man she's grieving, and he can't tell if it's for him or for someone else.

chapters.title: Children of the Cassiopeia
chapters.summary: The lost deep-space ship returns after forty years; its crew are children again, screaming about a signal that 'unmade' them. Ansel's POV shifts to forensic mode as he realizes one child wears the original's face. The emotional beat is vertigo—the murder victim may not be dead, just displaced in time.

chapters.title: Case File: A. Oyelaran
chapters.summary: Ansel breaks protocol and reads the sealed murder file, discovering the original had found evidence of temporal experiments beneath the colony. Corporate handler Voss contacts him remotely, ordering him home. The beat is betrayal: Ansel understands he was never investigating—he was sent to be erased alongside the evidence.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Following the child-crew's fragmented testimony, Ansel descends into the frozen excavation site below Meridian-9. His POV documents the weapon: a relay that broadcasts backward through time, rewriting whoever receives it. The beat is horror transformed into resolve—he realizes his own memory buffers were built from this same technology.

chapters.title: Sefa's Confession
chapters.summary: Sefa admits she helped the original hide the evidence and watched him die for it; she's been keeping the lights on so the relay couldn't fully wake. Her POV braids with Ansel's as they plan to reach the edge-of-dead-space transmitter. The beat is grief becoming partnership—two keepers of other people's secrets.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Corporate enforcers land to purge the colony and wipe Ansel's buffers; the child-crew scatter into the ice fields as decoys. Ansel's POV captures a desperate overland escape with Sefa, leaving the colonists to their evacuation ships. The beat is guilt sharpened into urgency—survival means abandoning the people he was sent to record.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Crossing the signal-dead zone on foot, Ansel's buffers begin failing, bleeding the original's memories into his own until he can't tell whose wife, whose crimes, whose fear he carries. The beat is identity dissolving: he must choose which man reaches the relay, knowing only one can survive the transmission.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: At the transmitter, Voss confronts them personally, revealing Ansel was cloned specifically because clones can carry the broadcast without being rewritten. Ansel triggers the upload anyway, broadcasting the truth to every colony in range as Voss tries to stop him. The beat is sacrifice: the transmission burns away everything the original ever was inside him.

chapters.title: An Unwritten Man
chapters.summary: Weeks later, colonies respond to the broadcast; the corporation fractures, and Meridian-9's survivors return. Ansel, stripped of inherited memory, stands before Sefa as a stranger who chose to stay. The final beat is quiet rebirth: he begins recording—not a case file, but his own life, in his own words, for the first time.
